summary: This is a Terminal component that displays shell commands and output with optional typewriter animation. It handles copying text to clipboard, auto-scaling animation speed based on content length, and resolves variable substitutions. The animation only starts when the terminal scrolls into view, and users can click to skip it.

explanations.30: This defines a type alias for a Map that stores React element types (like heading functions) as keys and their corresponding markdown prefixes (like '# ' for h1) as values.
explanations.32: This function recursively extracts all text content from a React component tree, handling arrays, strings, and nested elements. It reconstructs the original text by joining parts together and adding separators between items.
explanations.40: The function recursively processes each child element in an array, building up text one child at a time.
explanations.48: Since TypeScript doesn't know this object is a React element, we explicitly tell it with a type assertion so we can safely access the element's props.
explanations.50: This looks up the element's type in the map to get any prefix it needs (like '#' for headings), defaulting to an empty string if not found.
explanations.52: If the child is a Fragment, we use an empty separator to avoid adding line breaks between its contents; otherwise we use a newline to separate children.
explanations.61: This function returns different animation speeds and delays based on how many lines the terminal has, so shorter terminals animate faster and longer ones slower.
explanations.109: This hook gets the current variable resolver from context, which is used throughout the component to substitute variable placeholders with their actual values.
explanations.117: MDX components are fetched from context so we can build a mapping of heading component functions to their markdown prefixes.
explanations.118: This creates a map once per render (only when mdxComponents changes) that connects each heading component to its prefix, so getCopyText can later recover the '#' symbols that MDX strips.
explanations.132: Before anything else happens, we resolve all variable substitutions in the children once, so copy, animation, and rendering all use the same resolved tree.
explanations.145: We extract and split the text into lines once when the typewriter mode activates, capturing that snapshot so the animation finishes with its original text even if the user edits variables mid-animation.
explanations.152: We calculate the effective animation speed by preferring explicit props, but falling back to auto-scaled speeds based on line count.
explanations.163: This effect sets up an observer to detect when the terminal scrolls into view, so the animation only starts when it's actually visible to the user.
explanations.171: IntersectionObserver is a browser API that efficiently watches when an element enters the viewport; we check if it exists to handle server-side rendering safely.
explanations.199: We get the current line being animated from the animLines array using the current line index.
explanations.200: This regex checks if a line is a command line by looking for optional whitespace followed by a shell prompt character ($ or #).
explanations.202: Command lines are typed character-by-character, so we schedule the next character to appear after the effective speed delay.
explanations.208: Empty lines get a shorter pause (80ms) than regular output lines, which use the calculated effective delay.
explanations.234: We get the text to copy from the resolved children, which includes any variable substitutions the user has made.
explanations.236: If copyCommandOnly is true, we filter to only command lines and strip the prompt prefix, making the result directly pasteable into a shell.
explanations.257: For animation display, we combine all already-revealed lines with a partial slice of the current line being typed, creating the in-progress animation view.
explanations.263: This boolean tracks whether an animation is currently running, used to decide cursor style and click handling.
explanations.296: The 'ghost' span renders the complete final content invisibly behind the animation overlay, preventing the terminal from resizing as each line types out.
